kicker: Architectures: attention and the KV cache

scenes.headline: How attention shrinks the cache it rereads every step
scenes.sub: MHA, MQA, GQA and MLA, counted in bytes
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Larch! Every new token rereads a cache of past keys and values. Here's how attention learned to shrink it.

scenes.text: Decoding rereads every cached key and value at every step, so bytes set the speed. Each variant caches fewer bytes per token.
scenes.say: Decoding rereads the whole cache at every step, so its size sets the speed. Each variant caches fewer bytes per token.

scenes.title: The bill, per token and layer
scenes.text: cache = 2 x n_kv x d_h x bytes

parts.say: Every token keeps a key and a value.

parts.note: MHA: one per query head. GQA: a few. MQA: one.
parts.say: The lever is the number of key-value heads: one per query head, a few groups, or just one.
Times the head width, times two bytes in sixteen-bit.

steps.say: Multi-head attention gives every query head its own key and value head. That's the full bill.
Grouped-query attention lets each group of query heads share one. On T5, eight groups kept nearly all the quality.
Multi-query shares one across all heads: the smallest cache, and the biggest quality cost.

scenes.title: MLA: cache a latent, not the heads

steps.say: MLA squeezes each token's hidden state into one latent of five hundred and twelve numbers.
Only the latent is cached, and all one hundred and twenty-eight heads share it.
Rotary position can't survive the compression, so a separate sixty-four wide key carries it.

steps.note: 576 numbers: nine halves of a head width
steps.say: At attention time the up-projections fold into the query and output. Keys are never rebuilt.

scenes.title: One 128K sequence, DeepSeek-V2's shape
scenes.say: At a hundred and twenty-eight K tokens, the full multi-head cache is fifty-seven times MLA's: four hundred and eighty against eight and a half.

scenes.text: The queries never change; only the key-value side shrinks, by sharing heads or by caching a compressed latent.
scenes.say: The queries never change. Only the key-value side shrinks: share its heads, or cache a latent and rebuild nothing.

recap: Cache per token per layer: 2 x heads x width
GQA shares heads; MLA compresses them
MLA: 576 numbers, MHA quality in DeepSeek's tests
scenes.say: Count the key-value heads. Share them, or compress them. And check the bytes at your context length.
